items.why: Three atone entries (mist-20261102-142233-82, mist-20261023-193439-69, mist-20261008-145106-69) each record the same mistake across independent projects while the registered check shows zero fires in the same period.

proposal.change: Audit why the script produces zero fires and change its exit code to 1 so it blocks the turn instead of exiting silently when the answer to an owner ask is already present in notes or memory.

happened.what: Listed Clanky's own accounts as a blocker on you when the project notes already answered which accounts existed.
Asked you for a Speedway login and created a new test account when the project notes already had the login details.

items.why_repeats: The check registered to stop Claude from asking questions whose answers are already derivable has not fired once in the last fourteen days, so nothing has stopped any of these occurrences.
items.fix: The check's matching logic needs to be fixed and its exit mode changed to blocking so it stops the turn rather than running silently when notes or memory already contain the answer Claude is about to ask for.

items.title: Asked you for something already written down in your own notes
items.why: Three atone entries (mist-20261102-142233-82, mist-20261023-193439-69, mist-20261008-145106-69) each record the same mistake across independent projects while the registered check shows zero fires in the same period.

proposal.change: Audit why the script produces zero fires and change its exit code to 1 so it blocks the turn instead of exiting silently when the answer to an owner ask is already present in notes or memory.

happened.what: Asked you which backend pairs with each frontend and shipped a literal question-mark placeholder when the app's own code already answered it.

items.why_repeats: The check's output contract specifies exit 0 on every path, so it has never been able to block a turn regardless of whether it fires; additionally the check only inspects whether a code-reading tool ran in the current turn and cannot see whether the answer is in project notes, which is the source for two of the three instances.
items.fix: Change the exit code from 0 to 1 when the check fires so it blocks the turn before the question reaches you; the two notes-based instances (accounts listed as a blocker, login details already in project notes) are outside this check's scope entirely and need a separate gate that consults notes or memory before allowing the question through.

guard.plain: A check that is supposed to stop Claude from asking you for something it could have looked up itself, but it is wired to exit silently on every path and only checks whether Claude read code before asking — it cannot see whether the answer already exists in project notes
guard.gap: The check exits with code 0 on every path including when it fires, so it can never block a turn; its matching logic covers code-reading tools only, leaving the two notes-based instances entirely outside its scope
